Avery — quick triage from Deal Desk after reviewing the term sheet and benchmarking to similar pilots:

Summary of high-risk items:
- Price-comparison guarantee (the clause intends to force us to match any lower price offered elsewhere for 12 months). This is functionally a broad price promise with open-ended discovery risk. High revenue/leakage exposure.
- Prioritized access / exclusivity window for NA model variants for 6 months. Operationally possible but limits our ability to schedule capacity for other customers; creates unfair precedence unless we cap duration and scope.
- Automatic discount tied to a performance benchmark (token cost threshold). This is tricky because it transfers measurement and dispute resolution burden to Redwood and could trigger retroactive credits.

Recommended internal path (Deal Desk):
1) Replace price-comparison guarantee with a capped "price protection" commitment: if we lower published list pricing for the same SKU within the first 6 months, Solstice can request a one-time one-step reduction (not an open promise to match any custom discount).
2) Approve prioritized access for a 3-month pilot window limited to the "pilot" model variant list + a traffic cap; include carveouts for pay-as-you-go bursts.
3) Remove automatic retroactive discounts tied to raw token benchmarks. Offer instead a quarterly remediation process: if measured throughput or error rates exceed thresholds, the parties follow a defined remediation plan and may agree a one-off credit by mutual written consent.

Why this needs escalation: the original language as-written creates ongoing price exposure and operational scheduling risk beyond standard pilot terms. If execs want to approve the broader 12-month parity promise and automatic benchmark credits we need explicit authorization to accept potential revenue impact and operational constraints.

Attachments: redwood_comp_scope_matrix.xlsx (internal sensitivity scoring)

Ben
Senior Deal Desk Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Legal note — suggested redlines and risk points

Team — I reviewed the Solstice draft and Ben's notes. High-level legal concerns:
- The price-comparison/market-parity language is written broadly and lacks: (a) scope of competitor set; (b) whether the comparison includes promotional/volume deals; (c) an upper bound on remedies. We should not accept an automatic match or open-ended retro credits.
- The prioritized access provision effectively creates a soft exclusivity: it references "priority access to latest variants" without geographic, SKU, or capacity carveouts. That could hamper future sales and complicate capacity planning.
- Benchmark-triggered credits are poorly defined (who measures, what constitutes a breach, dispute resolution).

Redline recommendations (attached):
- Narrow market parity: define comparable offers (publicly published equivalent SKU), limit to 6 months, and make any remedy a one-time customer-initiated credit limited to X% of monthly spend (TBD by Finance).
- Convert prioritized access into a "preferred routing" arrangement for the pilot period with explicit traffic caps, explicit scheduling windows, and a clause that allows Redwood to re-route if production emergencies occur.
- Replace automatic benchmark credits with a defined SLA + remediation matrix; credits only after mutual confirmation of metrics and capped at a fixed dollar amount.

If Deal Desk and Sales want to accept broader language (12-month parity or an automatic benchmark credit mechanism) we need an exec-level policy exception signed off by Pricing Lead and VP Sales.

I've attached a redlined term sheet to speed negotiation: solstice_term_sheet_v3_redline.pdf

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

TL;DR: Solstice is asking for pilot-level prioritized access and a broad price-comparison protection + benchmark-triggered discounts. Deal Desk and Legal recommend restricting those asks and want exec approval for any deviation from the redlines below.

Concrete recommended approvals (we seek one combined decision):
1) Approve a pilot concession: 3 months of prioritized routing for named pilot SKUs, capped to 250k tokens/day and only within NA. Operational carveouts (emergency re-routing) remain.
2) Approve a limited price-protection concession: if Redwood reduces public list price for an equivalent SKU within first 6 months, customer is eligible to request a single, one-step price adjustment (not an automatic match). Cap the remedy at 15% of monthly committed spend for the pilot term.
3) Reject open-ended automatic benchmark credits. Approve a quarterly performance review and remediation pathway; allow a one-time good-faith credit by mutual written agreement capped to $25k for the pilot.

If you approve the three items above, Sales will accept the Solstice pilot and push forward signature on the redlined term sheet (attached). If you prefer to approve the customer's original asks (12-month parity or automatic benchmark-triggered credits), please reply explicitly — we will flag the expected financial/operational exposure in the final authorization and coordinate Finance signoff.

Requested by: end of business (PST) tomorrow, 2028-12-05, because procurement at Solstice is working to finalize their pilot purchase order.
